words.def: one tenth of what a person earns, given to support the church
words.ex: Every harvest, the farmer gave a tithe of his grain to the church.

words.def: to officially shut someone out of a church and its ceremonies
words.ex: In the Middle Ages, the pope could excommunicate a king who disobeyed him.

words.def: to check or prove that something is true or correct
words.ex: The scientists ran the test again to validate their results.

words.def: the substance that dissolves in a liquid to make a solution
words.ex: In salt water, the salt is the solute and the water does the dissolving.

words.def: to hold someone's whole attention
words.ex: A good mystery can engross me for hours.

words.def: a person who boasts too much
words.ex: Nobody enjoyed sitting next to the braggart who kept talking about his trophies.

words.def: the amount of money spent on something
words.ex: The town's biggest expenditure this year was repairing the roads.

words.def: support, especially money, given by a wealthy person to artists or a cause
words.ex: Thanks to the duke's patronage, the painter could spend years on one ceiling.

words.def: the feeling or idea a word suggests beyond its basic meaning
words.ex: The word "home" has a warm connotation.

words.def: a guard who stands watch
words.ex: A lone sentinel paced the castle wall all night.

words.def: the tendency of an object to keep doing what it is doing until a force acts on it
words.ex: Because of inertia, you lurch forward when the bus stops suddenly.

words.def: in the Middle Ages, land a lord gave to a knight in return for loyalty and service
words.ex: The king granted the brave knight a fief with a village and three farms.

words.def: a person in the Middle Ages who received land from a lord in return for loyalty
words.ex: The vassal promised to serve the lord faithfully.

words.def: to choose not to do or take something
words.ex: Three members decided to abstain from the vote.

words.def: a huge cloud of gas and dust in space where stars can form
words.ex: Through the telescope, the nebula looked like a glowing pink cloud.

words.def: fierce, tireless energy for a cause or goal you believe in
words.ex: She cleaned her room with surprising zeal.

words.def: to return to a former state or habit
words.ex: After vacation, I revert to waking up early.

words.def: to cut into two equal parts
words.ex: Draw a line to bisect the square into two rectangles.

words.def: writing that uses humor to make fun of foolish behavior or ideas
words.ex: The class newspaper printed a satire about endless homework.

words.def: to make a job be done by machines or computers instead of by people
words.ex: The factory will automate the packing line so robots box the cereal.

words.def: to stretch something out so it reaches further
words.ex: The artist chose to elongate the figures so they looked tall and graceful.

words.def: to dry out with great heat
words.ex: The desert sun can parch the ground until it cracks.

words.def: one of the two days each year when day and night are about the same length
words.ex: On the spring equinox, the sun shines for about twelve hours.

words.def: very delicious
words.ex: Grandma's delectable peach pie disappeared fast.

words.def: to make or become stronger
words.ex: The storm began to intensify as it moved toward the coast.

words.def: to make fun of someone in a loud, rude way
words.ex: Good fans do not jeer at the other team.

words.def: great bravery, especially in battle
words.ex: The soldier won a medal for his valor.

words.def: having a good-natured, easygoing personality that makes people like you
words.ex: The amiable bus driver greeted every student by name.

words.def: great joy and celebration shared by many
words.ex: There was jubilation in the streets when the war ended.

words.def: a skilled public speaker
words.ex: The orator held the crowd's attention for an hour.

words.def: so interesting that you cannot stop paying attention
words.ex: The story was so riveting that I read it in one night.

words.def: extreme exaggeration used for effect
words.ex: Saying you have a million chores is hyperbole.

words.def: gas, heat or light that is sent out into the air
words.ex: Old cars produce more smoke emission than new ones.

words.def: the main character in a story
words.ex: The protagonist of the book is a girl who builds robots.

words.def: a fast, rushing stream of water
words.ex: The melting snow became a roaring torrent.

words.def: a connection between two things that change together
words.ex: There is a correlation between practice time and test scores.

words.def: a law that requires people to join the armed forces
words.ex: During the war, conscription forced young men to serve in the army.

words.def: a certificate or qualification that proves a person is trained for a job
words.ex: A teaching license is the main credential a school asks new teachers to show.

words.def: having to do with the movement of blood through the heart and blood vessels
words.ex: The heart is the pump at the center of the circulatory system.

words.def: to suggest a possible explanation that can be tested
words.ex: We hypothesize that plants will grow faster in sunlight.

words.def: to combine ideas from different sources into one whole
words.ex: Try to synthesize the facts from all three articles in your report.

words.def: to get something, often with special effort
words.ex: The coach worked hard to procure new uniforms for the team.

words.def: having to do with motion
words.ex: A rolling ball has kinetic energy.

words.def: a unit used to measure how loud a sound is
words.ex: The sound meter showed the decibel level climbing as the band played louder.

words.def: made of only one cell
words.ex: An amoeba is a unicellular creature that you can see only under a microscope.

words.def: to do better than or go faster than
words.ex: Her reading skills soon began to outstrip those of the older students.

words.def: a collection of wild or unusual animals
words.ex: The farm kept a menagerie of llamas, peacocks and pot-bellied pigs.

words.def: the special role or job a living thing has in its ecosystem
words.ex: The woodpecker's niche is to dig insects out of tree bark.

words.def: an agreement by both sides in a war to stop fighting
words.ex: The armistice was signed at eleven o'clock, and the guns fell silent.

words.def: a wide view of a whole area
words.ex: From the tower we saw a panorama of the whole city.

words.def: a person who worked to end slavery
words.ex: The abolitionist gave speeches calling for freedom for all.

words.def: a hidden danger or problem that is easy to fall into
words.ex: A common pitfall in math is forgetting to check your work.

words.def: the jellylike material that fills a cell around its parts
words.ex: Many chemical reactions happen in the cytoplasm.

words.def: to name things one by one in a list
words.ex: Can you enumerate the steps of the water cycle?

words.def: flat land beside a river that is covered with water when the river overflows
words.ex: Farmers grow rich crops on the floodplain because the river leaves fertile mud behind.

words.def: to claim that something is true, usually that someone did wrong, without proving it yet
words.ex: The neighbors allege that the dog dug up their flower beds.

words.def: a group of soldiers stationed in a fort or town to guard it
words.ex: A small garrison of fifty soldiers guarded the frontier fort.

words.def: relying on each other to survive or work
words.ex: Bees and flowers are interdependent.

words.def: a small early sample of something to come
words.ex: The warm afternoon was a foretaste of the summer ahead.

words.def: a piece of iron that becomes magnetic only while electricity flows through wire wrapped around it
words.ex: The junkyard crane used an electromagnet to lift crushed cars and drop them.

words.def: a tax on goods brought in from another country
words.ex: The tariff made imported shoes more expensive.

words.def: lacking skill; clumsy and unable to do something well
words.ex: The inept magician dropped every card he tried to hide.

words.def: the belief that buying more and more goods is good, or a way of life built around shopping
words.ex: The pastor warned that consumerism can make people care more about things than about others.

words.def: the wide mouth of a river where fresh water meets salt water
words.ex: Many young fish grow up in the estuary.

words.def: a metal made by melting two or more metals together
words.ex: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.

words.def: a short, interesting story about a real event
words.ex: Grandpa told an anecdote about his first job.

words.def: a short mention in writing of a well-known story, event or character
words.ex: The poem makes an allusion to an old fairy tale about a glass slipper.

words.def: something that causes a reaction
words.ex: A bright light is a stimulus that makes your pupils shrink.

words.def: the act of a region formally breaking away from a country
words.ex: The vote for secession split the nation in two.

words.def: to write out in full something that was spoken or written elsewhere
words.ex: The secretary had to transcribe the meeting from a recording.

words.def: to add something at the end of a piece of writing
words.ex: Please append a list of your sources to the end of the essay.

words.def: the traits of a living thing that you can see, such as color or height
words.ex: Two plants can have the same phenotype but different genes.

words.def: a layer of underground rock or soil that holds water
words.ex: The town gets its drinking water from an aquifer.

words.def: round and plump
words.ex: The rotund snowman wore a red scarf.

words.def: the right to vote
words.ex: The campaign for women's suffrage lasted many years.

words.def: the variety of living things in a place
words.ex: Rainforests have amazing biodiversity.

words.def: an idea or opinion formed before you have real knowledge or experience
words.ex: Her preconception that the new girl was shy vanished when they met.

words.def: an old instrument used to measure the height of the sun or stars to help sailors find their position
words.ex: The sailor held up his astrolabe to measure the angle of the North Star.

words.def: a substance that changes during a chemical reaction
words.ex: In this experiment, vinegar is one reactant and baking soda is the other.

words.def: barely enough; too small in amount
words.ex: The hikers shared their scanty supply of water until they found a stream.

words.def: an ordinary citizen of ancient Rome
words.ex: A plebeian could not join the senate in early Rome.

words.def: the growth of cities as more people move there from the countryside
words.ex: Urbanization emptied many farms as families moved to the city for factory jobs.

words.def: a tool sailors used to find their position from the sun and stars
words.ex: The captain held up a sextant to check the ship's position.

words.def: a change from a solid straight into a gas without melting first
words.ex: Dry ice shrinks by sublimation, giving off foggy gas but no puddle.

words.def: the repeating of the same first sound in nearby words
words.ex: The phrase "silly snakes slither slowly" uses alliteration.

words.def: a way of thinking from the Renaissance that valued learning, ancient writings and human achievement
words.ex: Humanism led scholars to study the old Greek and Roman books again.

words.def: a narrow strip of land that connects two larger areas of land
words.ex: A canal was dug across the isthmus to join two oceans.

words.def: a farmer who works someone else's land and pays the owner with part of the crop
words.ex: The sharecropper gave half of his cotton harvest to the landowner each fall.

words.def: the process of boiling a liquid and cooling the steam to make a purer liquid
words.ex: Distillation can turn salty seawater into fresh water.

words.def: producing young from only one parent, without male and female cells joining
words.ex: A starfish can grow a whole new body from one arm through asexual reproduction.

words.def: a living thing that breaks down dead plants and animals
words.ex: A mushroom is a decomposer that returns nutrients to the soil.

words.def: the exact dictionary meaning of a word
words.ex: The denotation of "snake" is simply a long reptile with no legs.

words.def: to decide or settle something ahead of time
words.ex: The rules predetermine which team kicks off first.

words.def: hints in a story about what will happen later
words.ex: The author used foreshadowing when the dog growled at the stranger in chapter one.

words.def: made of many cells
words.ex: Unlike bacteria, a mushroom is multicellular and has many different cells.

words.def: an argument that opposes another argument
words.ex: A strong essay answers the counterclaim instead of ignoring it.

words.def: the science of naming living things and sorting them into groups
words.ex: In taxonomy, scientists sort every living thing from kingdom down to species.

words.def: the set of genes a living thing carries for a trait
words.ex: A pea plant's genotype decides whether it can pass on wrinkled seeds.

words.def: the lowest layer of the atmosphere, where we live and where weather happens
words.ex: Clouds, rain and storms all form in the troposphere.

words.def: a tiny part inside a cell that has a special job
words.ex: The nucleus is the largest organelle in many cells.

words.def: to burn slowly with smoke but no flame
words.ex: The campfire will smolder long after the flames die.

words.def: marked with spots or blotches of different colors
words.ex: The frog's mottled skin helped it hide among the leaves.

words.def: a little at a time
words.ex: They built the treehouse piecemeal, adding a board whenever they had time.

words.def: soaked through with water
words.ex: My sodden socks squished in my boots.

words.def: active in the daytime and resting at night
words.ex: Squirrels are diurnal, but raccoons come out at night.

words.def: a member of a rich, powerful family in ancient Rome
words.ex: The patrician owned a large house with a garden.
